messages.subject: Re: Assessing convergence of two different objects with MCMC chains of the same model
parts:
Assuming that the two objects you have are coda:::mcmc.list objects, which can be created in nimble using the option samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE, then MCMCvis should accept them fine when you combine them into a length-4 list of arrays of samples.  That is, assuming you have

class(samplesListAsCoda1)    ## [1] "mcmc.list"
class(samplesListAsCoda2)    ## [1] "mcmc.list"

class(samplesListAsCoda1[[1]])   ## [1] "mcmc"
class(samplesListAsCoda1[[2]])    ## [1] "mcmc"


Then you can convert them to (one single) list of numeric samples arrays as:


samplesListOfArrays <- list(
    as.matrix(samplesListAsCoda1[[1]]),
    as.matrix(samplesListAsCoda1[[2]]),
    as.matrix(samplesListAsCoda2[[1]]),
    as.matrix(samplesListAsCoda2[[2]])
)

class(samplesListOfArrays)   ## [1] "list"
class(samplesListOfArrays[[1]])    ## [1] "matrix" "array"

Then this should work fine:

MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(samplesListOfArrays)

Hope this helps,
Daniel


On Sat, Feb 19, 2022 at 4:55 AM Jaume Adria Badia Boher <jaum...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all!

I have a perhaps basic question but I have not been able to manage it so far, even after having tried some functions in the coda, MCMCvis and other packages.

I ran the exact same model with nimble two different times. In both, I set the model to run with two chains, so I ended up having two objects of results with two chains each. I am now interested in assessing convergence of all 4 chains together, but I cannot manage to find any functions that merge both objects into a 4-chain mcmc object that allows me to pass easy convergence functions like MCMCvis::MCMCtrace() or MCMCvis::MCMCsummary(). 

I suspect coda::mcmc.list() or runjags::combineMCMC should help in doing this. However, I am getting errors all the time, basically complaining about my result outputs not being MCMC objects when they are.

Could anybody give some advice on which approach I should take?

Thanks! I hope I made it understandable.

Have a good Saturday!
